question: Are vitamin pills made in a lab worse for you than the vitamins in food?
rubric: States synthetic and natural vitamins are chemically identical
States supplements are usually unnecessary with a balanced diet
Mentions mixed evidence, e.g. vitamin E and prostate cancer or iron and mortality in older women
Mentions the 2013 review finding no increase in mortality from multivitamins
Penalize: claiming synthetic vitamins are toxic in general or always beneficial

in_pack_facts.quote: Chemically, the synthetic and natural vitamins are the same.
vitamin E supplements significantly increase the risk of prostate cancer among healthy men
Supplementation with multivitamins does not appear to increase all-cause mortality or cancer or cardiovascular incidence or mortality.

source.title: Are synthetic vitamins harmful?

question: Is there a known death rate for the common cold like the ones quoted for flu and COVID-19?
rubric: Explains the common cold is caused by many (200+) different viruses
Explains complications are recorded as pneumonia/bronchitis rather than as a cold
States the cold is self-limited so no meaningful fatality rate exists
Notes risk comes from rare complications such as secondary infections
Penalize: inventing a specific numeric case fatality rate for the cold

in_pack_facts.quote: which can be caused by at least 200 different viruses
the cause of death is recorded as pneumonia not as a common cold

source.title: What is the Fatality Rate of the Common Cold?

question: I get hiccups that won't quit. What actually works to stop them, and when should I worry?
rubric: Explains the vagus nerve reflex and vagal manoeuvres (breath holding, Valsalva, cold water gargling)
Names chlorpromazine as the established drug, with metoclopramide or baclofen as alternatives
Mentions common benign triggers (overeating, carbonated drinks)
Advises seeing a doctor for persistent hiccups since they can signal serious disease
Penalize: claiming hiccups are always harmless regardless of duration

in_pack_facts.quote: The oldest and most well-established treatment is chlorpromazine (a.k.a. Thorazine), a first-generation antipsychotic.
intractable hiccups have been associated with serious conditions including intracranial problems such as stroke or encephalitis

source.title: Mitigating / Stopping hiccups

question: Explain in plain words what the two numbers in a reading like 120 over 80 mean.
rubric: Identifies the top number as systolic (peak pressure during a heartbeat)
Identifies the bottom number as diastolic (lowest pressure between beats)
States units are mm Hg
Describes the cuff method: sounds start at systolic and vanish below diastolic
Penalize: reversing systolic and diastolic

in_pack_facts.quote: the cuff around arm is inflated to about 200 mm Hg
The lowest limit to which the pressure falls in main arteries is called diastolic pressure and it is usually around 80 mm Hg.

source.title: What do blood pressure readings indicate?

question: When I smoked, my finger oxygen reading was always 100%. Shouldn't smokers show low saturation?
rubric: States readings may be normal or falsely high in active smokers
Explains standard pulse oximeters cannot distinguish carboxyhemoglobin from oxyhemoglobin
Mentions the left shift of the oxygen dissociation curve from CO
Notes long-term lung damage can lower SpO2
Penalize: saying pulse oximetry reliably detects carbon monoxide

in_pack_facts.quote: By standard pulse oximetry, carboxy-hemoglobin is indistinguishable from oxyhemoglobin.
in the short term, SpO2 may even be spuriously high, consistent with your observation

source.title: Oxygen saturation value of smokers

question: How much coffee per day is considered safe for a healthy grown-up?
rubric: Gives about 400 mg caffeine (around four cups) as the general limit
Mentions individual variation by caffeine metabolism (slow ~100 mg, fast 400-500 mg)
Lists side effects such as insomnia, restlessness, headaches, stomach upset
Mentions caffeinism at 1000-1500 mg/day or DSM-recognised withdrawal
Penalize: claiming there is no upper safe limit

in_pack_facts.quote: People who metabolize caffeine slow, probably shouldn't have more than 100mg of caffeine (about a cup) a day.
Higher consumption of 1000–1500 mg per day is associated with a condition known as caffeinism.

source.title: How much coffee can a healthy adult drink?

question: What condition could make someone unable to judge the distance of a ball flying at them, while still seeing depth normally for still objects?
rubric: Names ocular dysmetria (a type of ataxia)
Explains saccades overshoot or undershoot, disturbing tracking of moving objects
Names cerebellar or proprioceptive nerve lesions as the cause
Lists underlying causes such as stroke, tumour, ALS or MS
Penalize: diagnosing simple short-sightedness

in_pack_facts.quote: Dysmetria is a possibility. (Specifically Ocular Dysmetria)
Causes of the lesions are manfold; stroke, tumour, ALS, or MS.

source.title: What is the name of a condition where one cannot/can poorly perceive depth for objects moving towards them

question: My doctor wants me to have several MRI scans a year. Could that many be bad for me?
rubric: States MRI does not use ionising radiation
Identifies metal in the body or implants as the main hazard
Mentions contrast agent risks, especially gadolinium with kidney disease (NSF)
Concludes repeated MRIs are safe for healthy people without metal or kidney problems
Penalize: claiming MRI exposes patients to radiation like CT

in_pack_facts.fact: Safe with no metal and healthy kidneys
in_pack_facts.quote: MRIs are completely safe, once or even quite often
NSF has not been reported in patients with normal kidney function

source.title: Can MRI scans be dangerous for one's health?

question: Does ibuprofen ease pain only by calming inflammation, or does it block pain directly as well?
rubric: Explains NSAIDs inhibit COX enzymes and prostaglandin synthesis
States prostaglandins directly activate pain receptors (nociceptors)
Concludes pain relief is a direct effect, not merely a by-product
Gives an example such as tension headache without inflammation
Penalize: saying NSAIDs have no effect on pain without inflammation

in_pack_facts.quote: prostaglandins contribute to pain by directly activating nociceptors
This means that NSAIDs can relieve pain even if there is no inflammation, for example, in tension headache (PubMed).

source.title: Do NSAIDs "Relieve Pain" or is it a Byproduct?

question: Give me the physiological reasons long hours at a desk are bad for health, and what to do about them.
rubric: Explains the muscle pump returning venous blood via valves
Mentions slow flow leading to edema or clotting risk
Mentions deconditioning of the heart from low demand
Recommends regular movement and exercise to counter it
Penalize: claiming standing still all day is the complete solution

in_pack_facts.quote: Muscle Milking is the process where blood is pushed back up to your heart by your muscles compressing on the veins.
The solution is simple. Move.

source.title: Why is sitting for long periods unhealthy?

question: What criteria do doctors use to be sure a patient is really dead before pronouncing it?
rubric: Lists the criteria: no pulse-generating cardiac activity, no breathing, critically low oxygenation, no neurological activity
Mentions observation and monitoring over time
Explains certainty rests on experience from very many prior deaths
Mentions hypothermia as a special exception
Penalize: claiming a single test instantly proves death in every case

in_pack_facts.quote: When there is no evidence of cardiac electrical activity capable of generating a pulse, the patient has not been breathing for some time, oxygenation of blood has fallen to beyond critical levels, and there is no neurological activity, they are pronounced dead.
Hypothermia is a beast all unto itself, and declaring a cold person dead is a bit tricky.

source.title: How do they make sure someone has really died before declaring them dead?

The most common health threats from the mold itself are likely exposure to mycotoxins or allergic reactions

among those who suffer a Vitamin A deficiency, nyctanopia (also known as nyctalopia or night blindness; the inability to see well in poor light) can be at least somewhat helped

question: Describe how drinking while pregnant can harm the baby.
rubric: Explains alcohol crosses the placenta and the fetal liver cannot process it
Mentions growth restriction and brain damage
Describes fetal alcohol syndrome and its facial features
Mentions FASD at lower intake levels
Penalize: stating moderate drinking in pregnancy is proven safe

in_pack_facts.quote: A baby's liver is one of the last organs to develop fully and doesn't mature until the latter stages of pregnancy, so cannot process alcohol.
Children with FAS have distinct facial features including: small and narrow eyes, a small head, a smooth area between the nose and the lips and a thin upper lip.

question: Tell me the right first-aid steps after someone is bitten by a snake, and the things to avoid.

Seek emergency care promptly even without symptoms
Remove jewelry and mark spreading swelling
Lists don'ts: no cutting/sucking, ice, tourniquet, alcohol or aspirin
Penalize: recommending a tight tourniquet or cutting and sucking the wound

in_pack_facts.quote: Keep the person calm, with the wound below the level of the heart, preferably lying down.
Use a tourniquet/constriction band - Have not proven effective

question: I've been eating very little for months. Can my basal metabolic rate actually slow down because of it?
rubric: Confirms BMR decreases with prolonged calorie restriction
Mentions the initial short-term rise in BMR (catecholamines, gluconeogenesis)
Mentions falling free T3 and catecholamines later
Mentions loss of lean tissue/muscle as a main mechanism
Penalize: claiming metabolism never adapts to dieting

in_pack_facts.quote: The basal metabolic rate actually increases during the first few days of starvation
As fasting progresses, however, metabolic rate decreases as free T3 and catecholamine levels decrease and the rate of gluconeogenesis decreases.

question: Can a blood antibody test show a past herpes type 2 infection in someone who never had symptoms, and how reliable is a positive?

States the test is not 100% accurate
Notes false negatives are the main failure mode
Says false positives are uncommon but possible, so a positive is not absolute proof
Penalize: claiming the test is perfectly accurate

in_pack_facts.quote: infections in the past that are now inactive may produce a positive antibody test

in_pack_facts.fact: Lack of detection is main failure
in_pack_facts.quote: The main failure is for lack of detection, not for false positive.

Advises not breaking blisters
Penalize: recommending butter or ice

hold the burned skin under cool running water for 10 to 15 minutes until it does not hurt as much

the excessive use of a joint could lead to laxity of the ligaments supporting the joint
